title: Knowledge Memory Claim
description: One immutable, identified assertion distilled from a conversation or record: subject, property, value, valid time, speaker/source and epistemic posture as typed fields. `posture` is how the speaker asserted it (stated / proposed / hypothetical / retracted); it is not the claim's review state, which is derived from its routing decision and any Survey review (see memory-routing-decision.schema.json). Field names follow the Surface knowledge-accumulation decision (kontourai/surface@7486c6d, docs/decisions/knowledge-accumulation.md): a subject is a (type, id) reference; a property slot is the subject plus `claimType`, `property` (Surface's `fieldOrBehavior`) and canonical `qualifiers`; `validTime` is a half-open interval [from, until) that is neither Surface's inclusive authority-trace `validUntil` nor `expiresAt` freshness; `supersedes` edges are `correction` or `succession` with a reason. Those interval and edge shapes are proposed there pending Hachure, so this schema carries them as caller-owned fields and is not a Hachure bundle. `id` is the sha256 digest of the claim's content (subject, claimType, property, qualifiers, value, validTime, speaker, posture, supersedes, audience, source.ref), recomputed on read; values compare by structural JSON equality, so a different spelling is a different claim. The evidence fields (source.locator, excerpt, observedAt, role, extractor) are not part of identity. A revision is a new claim with a new id.

claimType.description: Surface's claimType. The Kit assigns knowledge.memory-claim.

qualifiers.description: Surface canonical qualifiers; part of the slot. The extractor does not produce them yet, so slots are coarser than Surface's and conflict more readily.

value.description: Any JSON value. Equality is structural JSON equality.

validTime.description: Half-open interval [from, until) of when the assertion says the value held in the world. Absent bounds are unbounded; an absent validTime asserts no bound. Instants are ISO 8601 dates or zoned date-times; an empty or unparseable interval is rejected, never guessed.

speaker.description: Who asserted it, as named in the source.

ref.description: Stable source identity, for example a sitting id.

excerpt.description: Verbatim quote the extractor grounded the claim in.

role.description: Role of the turn the claim was grounded in.

audience.description: Principals allowed to see the claim. Absent means it inherits its source's audience; omission never widens.
